Update: Nov 4th, 2026 11:55 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Jude Bellingham has been collecting Champions League records almost as enthusiastically as Real Madrid collect European trophies. And now he’s taking another one from a club legend (assuming no warming up injury).
 The England midfielder’s appearance against AEK Athens on Wednesday makes him the youngest player ever to reach 60 Champions League games , overtaking former Los Blancos goalkeeper Iker Casillas.
 🏛️ Champions League night in Athens. pic.twitter.com/92S7Lf91pU 
— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 4, 2026 
 How has Bellingham broken Iker Casillas’s Champions League record?
 Bellingham reaches the 60-game milestone aged 23 years and 128 days, beating Casillas, who was 23 years and 167 days old when he made his 60th appearance.
 That’s a difference of just 39 days , but enough to rewrite a record that had survived for more than two decades.
 This isn’t the first time Bellingham has taken an appearance record from Casillas. In November 2025, he became the youngest player to reach 50 Champions League games , achieving that milestone at 22 years and 128 days, also against the legendary Spanish goalkeeper’s previous benchmark.
 📋✅ Our starting XI.
🆚 @AEK_FC_OFFICIAL pic.twitter.com/5X4jpeJptJ 
— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 4, 2026 
 What other Champions League records does Jude Bellingham hold?
 Bellingham’s European adventure began with Borussia Dortmund in October 2020, when he was just 17.
 He became the youngest Englishman to start a Champions League game and later the youngest English scorer in the competition , netting against Manchester City aged 17 years and 289 days.
 He also became the youngest player to score as captain in a Champions League game , achieving the feat for Dortmund.
 And, of course, he already has a winner’s medal, having helped Real Madrid lift the trophy in 2024.
